scope: V4B-12 / C0 Passive stabilization publication notes
decision: A: approve the current C0 full note and short note as presented in the preceding review (overlay v0.6 text, unchanged since overlay v0.2). Full note: “Note. 'Passive' does not require that the system has no sensing or action pathways, that such pathways cannot be told apart, or that they have not been identified; whether they exist, can be distinguished and have been identified are separate questions. C0 is not exclusive with C1 (negative feedback) or C2 (specific regulation): they can be attributed in the same system, for example where binding relaxations occur alongside feedback-based adaptation. A stable state should not be read back as a set point or goal, passive relaxation should not be equated with sensing, and whole-system stability is not inferred. What mechanistic restriction 'passive' places on an individual decay route is left open.” Short note: “'Passive' ≠ 'no pathways' or 'pathways unidentified'. Not exclusive with C1/C2. See note.” Kept: existence, distinguishability and identification of sensing/action pathways handled separately; no exclusivity of C0 with C1/C2; co-attribution within one system not confused with classification of an individual decay route; no automatic inference of set point, goal or whole-system stability from C0; the mechanistic restriction of 受動的 (O-027-3) stays unresolved

scope: V4B-12 / OV-NOTE-INTERVENTION (shared by R0, Fc, M1)
decision: A: approve the current shared intervention full note and short note as presented in the preceding review (overlay v0.6 text, unchanged since overlay v0.3). Full note: “Intervention. In the source-faithful publication layer, intervention is treated as an assessment route, not automatically as a constitutive condition of R0, Fc or M1. It can test a relation under a declared intervention design and comparison conditions. A relation is not generally absent merely because no intervention was performed or because its causal path was not fully traced. A null result from a single intervention does not, by itself, establish the general absence of the relation; its evidential significance depends on the intervention design and declared comparison conditions. Being open to intervention is distinct from having been established by a particular intervention. The English reconstruction may retain layer-specific intervention requirements, including D-H4 for Fc.” Short note: “In the source-faithful publication layer, intervention is an assessment route, not automatically a constitutive condition; a single null result is scope-dependent.” Approved reading: in the Japanese source-faithful publication layer intervention is an assessment route; no inference of absence from non-performance of an intervention or an unidentified causal path alone; a single null result does not by itself prove general absence but can count against the relation under specified conditions; intervenability distinguished from demonstration by a particular intervention; English reconstruction-layer conditions not identified with publication-layer conditions. Boundaries: R0, Fc and M1 constitutive conditions unchanged; D-H4 and conditional reconstruction proposals unchanged in effect
